paper.title: OpenHLM: An Empirical Recipe for Whole-Body Humanoid Loco-Manipulation

review.question: 2025-07-19 至 2026-07-19 的 loco-manipulation 研究在哪些控制、学习、数据、感知、评测和部署方向取得了可验证进展，其适用边界与未解问题是什么？

relevance.reason: A very recent empirical roadmap for native whole-body humanoid VLA design, data collection and heterogeneous co-training.

sections_read.purpose: Identify limits of decoupled humanoid control.

sections_read.locator: 3 Building a Whole-Body Loco-Manipulation System: A Roadmap
sections_read.purpose: Inspect controller, VLA and data-design ablations.
Verify held-out task gains and data-source roles.
Record platform, data and architecture boundaries.

research_question: Which controller, teleoperation, VLA and heterogeneous-data choices make a native whole-body humanoid policy effective?
contributions: A controlled empirical roadmap and the 12-task HLM-12 real-robot benchmark.

method.summary: OpenHLM combines joint-space whole-body teleoperation, a humanoid-adapted VLA and co-training with stationary teleoperation or robot-free HuMI data.
assumptions: A task-aligned whole-body controller and modest on-robot demonstrations are available.
Cheap data streams can be aligned to the humanoid action and visual interfaces.

study_context.sample_or_scale: Twelve benchmark tasks, generally five physical rollouts per policy-task pair, plus a long-horizon system comparison.

evaluation.design: One-variable-at-a-time real-robot ablations compare teleoperation interfaces, action/model choices and heterogeneous co-training; two humanoid VLAs are system-level baselines.

findings.finding: Cheap same-embodiment manipulation data extended the VLA to held-out objects, prompts and a new manipulation motion without additional whole-body teleoperation.
findings.scope: Four HLM-12 tasks held out from whole-body teleoperation on a single humanoid.

author_stated.limitation: Results use one G1 platform and limited scenes; HuMI data does not yet teach novel motion as effectively as on-robot data, and architectural mechanisms remain underexplained.

reader_inferred.boundary: The roadmap is strong within-system evidence, but not a universal ranking of all humanoid VLA architectures.
reader_inferred.basis: Most findings come from one platform, benchmark and implementation stack.

transfer_boundary: Supports native whole-body action spaces and heterogeneous co-training when at least some embodiment-specific demonstrations anchor the policy.

design_strengths: Controlled real-robot ablations across the full stack.
Held-out tasks distinguish semantic transfer from new-motion transfer.
design_risks: Five rollouts per pair produce wide uncertainty.
critical_appraisal.baseline_fairness: System baselines receive matched demonstration counts, while OpenHLM changes the source mix as the method under test.
critical_appraisal.metric_validity: Task progress reveals partial long-horizon completion but is benchmark-specific.
critical_appraisal.reproducibility: The paper promises code, data and checkpoints and reports detailed protocols.
critical_appraisal.external_validity: Limited to Unitree G1 and HLM-12.

evidence_cards.claim: On four tasks held out from whole-body teleoperation, stationary same-embodiment co-training raised average task progress from 33% to 87%, close to a 94% 12-task teleoperation oracle.
evidence_cards.relation: Supports heterogeneous co-training as a practical way to extend native whole-body VLAs.
evidence_cards.summary: The paper overview reports the held-out-task gain and the full-teleoperation oracle.
evidence_cards.source_context: Quantitatively, OpenHLM reaches 89% average task progress on the 8 training tasks of our HLM-12 benchmark; on the remaining 4 held-out tasks that whole-body teleop never covers, co-training with cheaper data lifts task progress from 33% to 87%, closing most of the gap to a 12-task oracle (94%).

verification.rationale: The section states the held-out task count, baseline and co-training values; the oracle value is reported in the introduction for the same held-out set.
